unit: Unit 12: Everyday Life with Your Computer
title: Notes and Documents
drDigitalIntro:
Your computer comes with a notes app. It is good for quick lists and ideas, and it saves by itself.
• Find it: it is called Notes on a Mac, Notepad on Windows. Search your apps for it.
• Make a new note (look for a + or a New button) and type a short list of your own: three things you actually need this week.
• Notice there is no Save button to press. It keeps your words on its own.
• Then use two skills from Unit 2: select your list and copy it (Ctrl+A then Ctrl+C), come back here, and paste it.
• I can tell the difference between pasted text and typed text, so the paste is the proof.

playgroundTask.goal: You wrote a real note in your own notes app and copied it out

steps.say: Open the notes app on your computer and start a new note.
steps.detail: Notes on a Mac, Notepad on Windows. Search your apps if you do not see it.

steps.say: Type a list of three things you need this week, in your own words.
steps.detail: Anything real: groceries, errands, birthdays. Three lines is plenty.

steps.say: Copy your list there, then paste it in the box below.
steps.detail: In the notes app: Ctrl+A to select all, Ctrl+C to copy (Command on a Mac). Click the box, then Ctrl+V. Typing it out by hand will not count; it has to arrive as a paste.

drDigitalSuccess: A real note, in your real notes app, copied between two programs. That is everyday computing, done. Your list is still sitting in the notes app whenever you need it.
drDigitalHint: The copy happens in the notes app; the paste happens here. Ctrl+A then Ctrl+C over there. Click the box here, then Ctrl+V.
